title: Settings & Advanced
markdown:
**What it is:** The settings that live outside the day-to-day nav: whether the Executive is running and how it sounds, who Open Executive is for, letting it write email as you, and the admin and power-user tools.

**What it does:**

- Opens on a page of tiles, one per settings page — **Your Executive**, **Workspace**, **Advanced** and **About**. Each tile says what's on its page and, where it can, how things stand now (running or paused, the voice, just you or your team, a newer version). Click a tile to open its page; the **Settings** link at the top of each page takes you back. Old links to a section (such as `/settings#workspace`) land on the matching page. **Act as me**, **Handle it for me** and **Take the lead** are not in Settings: they are the three tabs of **Delegate** in the main menu.
- **Your Executive** shows whether the Executive is **running** or **paused**, with one button: **Pause…** opens the pause form; while it is paused, who paused it, the held count and **Resume** stay in view. Below it, **Voice** picks the voice the Executive answers you in.
- **Workspace** holds, one card each: whether Open Executive is personal or for your team, your role when it's just you, your time zone, and whether the Executive books meetings without asking. **Company email domains** sits under **Advanced** at the bottom.
- **Act as me** (a tab of **Delegate** in the main menu) lets you have the Executive write email drafts as you, in your own voice, from your own Gmail — when you ask, and, if you turn it on, for mail in your inbox that needs you, which you can send from Home with one tap. Your mailbox and the two switches are up front; **How I write** (and, for the owner, **Let team members use it**) sit under **Advanced** at the bottom.
- **Advanced** lists the pages that open their own screen, grouped by what you'd use them for: **Check & diagnose** (Setup status, Audit log, Token usage), **Configure** (Agent Council, Company Simulator, Client Companies) and **Learn** (User Guide, Architecture).
- **About** shows the version this install runs, and whether a newer one is out.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Settings** at the bottom of the sidebar. (On a phone, open the menu with the button at the top left; Settings is at its bottom.)
2. Click a tile to open that page.
3. On **Advanced**, click a row to open that page:
   - **Setup status** — check that every part of your setup is working, and see what to do about anything that isn't.
   - **Agent Council** — change a specialist's model or prompt, or the Executive's voice.
   - **Audit log** — find out what the Executive did, and why.
   - **Token usage** — see what you're spending and where.
   - **User Guide** — this guide.
   - **Architecture** — the technical reference for how the system is built.
   - **Company Simulator** — try the Executive on a test company.
   - **Client Companies** — switch between clients if you do fractional work.

**Checking your setup:**

- Open **Settings → Advanced → Setup status**. Each part of your setup gets a light: green is working, amber needs attention, red isn't working, grey isn't set up (and is optional).
- It tests things for real: the AI key, and each chat app's token, with a quick call that sends nothing. It also checks the Executive's email address, the company setup, the daily schedule, when and where your daily brief goes, and whether anyone on your team list can reach each chat app.
- Anything that isn't green says what to do in plain words, with a button when the fix is on another page. After you change a setting and restart the app, click **Check again**.

**Workspace:**

- **Using Open Executive** — **Personal** or **Team**. You pick this when you first set up; change it here. Switching asks you to confirm and says what changes:
  - **Personal** pauses department check-ins and renames **Company** in the sidebar to **You**, with **Goals** (grouped by area), **People** and your profile — there is no Departments tab. Nothing is deleted — your departments stay, as the areas your goals are grouped by.
  - **Team** brings back **Company** with its **Departments** tab and their daily check-ins, and the People and Departments tiles on Home.
- **Your role** (just you) — which describes you best (**Owner / founder**, **Executive inside an organisation**, **Independent or fractional**, or **Other**), your title, who you report to, what you're responsible for and what you're measured on. Every field is optional; click **Save role** after editing. The Executive uses it to fit its advice to your job — a VP gets help making the case to their boss, an owner gets help with a call that's theirs alone to make. It stays saved if you switch to your team.
- **Time zone** — when your morning brief, end-of-day digest and reflection arrive, and how the Executive reads "tomorrow at 9". It suggests the zone your browser is in; **Follow server default** uses the server's setting.
- **Book meetings without asking** — when on, the Executive books meetings on your calendar on its own; when off, each booking waits for your approval on Home. (Shown only when your install supports it.)
- **Company email domains** (under **Advanced**, principal only) — mail from these domains matches a teammate by the part before the @, and a new address there is filled in as a teammate when someone writes in. It follows your own address unless you set it here.
- Only the principal can change the mode, role and time zone. A persona you customised in Council stays in place in either mode.

**Act as me (Delegate → Act as me):**

- Normally the Executive writes only as itself, from its own email account. **Act as me** lets it write an email *as you*: ask in chat — "reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th" — and it saves a draft in **your own Gmail Drafts** for you to read, change and send. Asking in chat never sends anything, and everything else it writes stays in its own name.
- The owner sees this page, and so does each team member once the owner turns on **Let team members use it** under **Advanced** at the bottom of it (shown only where your install allows it). Each team member connects their own Gmail and turns it on for themselves. What it reads in their mail, the drafts it writes and their **Replies waiting** are theirs alone: the owner sees only who uses it and how many drafts and sends it made, and a conversation in which it read someone's mail can be opened only by that person. Turning the owner's switch off takes it away from the team from their next message. It works when you ask in the web app, in a direct message to the Executive on Slack or Discord, or in a verified private Telegram chat — never in a shared channel or thread, from an email, a scheduled job or anyone else's conversation.
- **Your Gmail** — connect your own Gmail first. The page shows the command to run on a computer with a browser; sign in as yourself, put the file it writes where your install reads it, then click **Check again**. It won't connect the Executive's own address as yours.
- **Write drafts as me** — the switch. It stays off until your Gmail is connected, and turning it off applies from your next message.
- **Draft replies to my inbox** — a second switch, once **Write drafts as me** is on. Every few minutes the Executive looks at new mail in your inbox, and for mail that needs a personal reply from you — a question, a request, a meeting to arrange, an introduction or a follow-up — it writes a first reply in your Gmail Drafts and puts it at the top of **Needs you** on Home. Nothing is sent until you tap **Send** there. It only looks at mail that arrives after you turn it on, and leaves out newsletters, notifications, mailing lists, mail you've already answered and anything that doesn't need you; mail you answer within ten minutes never gets a draft. The first reply only acknowledges: it repeats only what you've already said in the thread, commits you to nothing and lists what's left for you to decide. Someone you've never written to gets a short holding reply. The line under the switch says how it's doing (for example, that your Gmail needs connecting again) and when it last looked; click **Check now** to look straight away. Turning **Write drafts as me** off turns this off too.
- **How I write** (under **Advanced**) — click **Learn from my sent mail** and it reads your recent sent emails once and describes how you write (click **Edit how I write** to open the fields): your usual **Length** and **Tone**, a **Greeting** for your team, your contacts and anyone else ({first} stands for their first name), your **Sign-off**, your **Habits**, what you **Never** do, and a few **Examples of your writing** that set the tone. Change any of them and click **Save changes**; **Lock** stops it being relearned from your mail (you can still edit it); **Reset** starts over; **Remove examples** drops the examples. Your Gmail signature is added to every draft: **Refresh from Gmail** picks up a change you made to it in Gmail, **Don't add my signature** stops adding it, and **Add my Gmail signature** brings it back.
- In chat you get a card, "Drafted an email as you to …", that opens the draft in Gmail. If the Executive isn't sure about something, it asks you instead of guessing.

**Setting up just for yourself:**

- The first time you set up, Open Executive asks who it is for — **Personal** or **Team** — before anything else, and saves your time zone from the browser. Re-running setup later skips this; change the mode here instead. Either way you can add teammates later from **People**.
- **Personal** is for anyone who uses Open Executive just for themselves, whatever their role: your own business, a team you lead inside an organisation, or clients you advise as an independent or fractional executive.
- Choosing **Personal** then asks **What's your role?** — the same fields as **Your role** above. Fill in what you like, or click **Skip for now**.
- Just for yourself, the setup conversation asks about your work rather than your team, following the role you gave: an owner about what you offer, your customers, pricing, cash and runway; an executive inside an organisation about that organisation (it becomes your company profile), what you're responsible for, who you report to and what you're measured on; an independent about your practice and clients. Everyone is asked about their goals. On **Here's what I understood** there is a single **You** card (your name and role) next to **Your sign-in email**, instead of the team and department lists.
- The step-by-step form skips the team size, team members and fractional executives steps.
- In the sidebar, **You** takes the place of **Company** and holds **Goals**, **People** and your profile: **Business profile** if you own the business, **Your work** for any other role (or none). The profile page follows the same choice: for any other role it is worded around the organisation you work in (**Where You Work** in place of Company Basics). Either way departments are listed there as **Areas**, and your title, who you report to and what you're responsible for stay under **Your role** above.

**Pausing the Executive:**

- Open **Settings → Your Executive** (or **Pause or resume the Executive** in the account menu — the **⋯** next to your name at the bottom of the sidebar) and click **Pause…**. Add a reason if you like, and click **Pause Executive**.
- While paused, the Executive starts nothing on its own: no briefs, nudges, monitoring, inbox processing or workflow timers. An amber banner appears on every page.
- Chat and direct messages (Slack, Telegram, Discord, Google Chat) still get answers.
- Nothing is lost. Work that falls due during the pause waits, and runs when you click **Resume**. The switch shows how many actions are waiting.
- Anyone who can sign in can pause the Executive, but only the principal can resume it.

*Tip: if you're looking for a feature that isn't in the sidebar, it's probably under **Settings → Advanced**. This guide is also in the account menu (the **⋯** next to your name at the bottom of the sidebar), with **Pause or resume the Executive** and, when you signed in with an account, **Sign out**.*
